desc: Establish the potential-label equivalence: fixed D is feasible iff the minimum number of edges with p(v)>p(u), subject to p(1)=0, p(N)=D, and p(v)≤p(u)+1, is at most K.

Derive and validate a polynomial fixed-D min-cut construction for minimizing the number of directed edges with p(v)>p(u), under p(1)=0, p(N)=D, 0≤p≤D, and p(v)≤p(u)+1; explicitly handle each original edge being charged exactly once.
Establish complexity bounds suitable for N ≤ 30, M ≤ 100 and identify the best practical implementation approach in Python.
Handle edge cases: direct parallel edges, zero attainable answer, cycles, and converting “at most K” feasibility into “exactly K” selection.
Produce a correctness proof outline and implementation details for the final stdin/stdout Python solution.
